rawRetro.summary: Repair 3: fixed the one root cause behind the B00 failure — the document record route was declared with the parent segment repeated. `client/routes.ts` registered `document-detail` with `path: '/documents/:id'`, and the app-client route resolver always prepends `'/'` to any child path before appending it to the parent (it strips leading slashes only to re-add one), so the real registered path became `/documents/documents/:id`. `/documents/:id` therefore never matched, fell through to the AppRouter wildcard `<Route path='*'>`, and redirected every document card click / assistant citation link to `/` (Home). The path is now the relative `':id'`, resolving to `/documents/:id`. A route-resolution test now pins the resolved path (`/documents/:id` present, `/documents/documents/:id` absent) so a repeat of the absolute-child-path mistake fails in CI rather than only in the browser. Verified: the record page opens over the list at `/documents/<id>`, a supervisor can read and edit C there, a colleague is refused C at the same normal URL (404-as-absent) and reads A, and the assistant citation link reaches the same page. Checks run: `vitest run` on `tests/logic/client-routes.test.ts` and `tests/logic/documents-pages.test.tsx` (10 tests pass), `tsc --noEmit` clean, `prettier --check` and `eslint` clean on the two changed files. Previous repairs remain in force (see prior summary below). Prior repair 2 summary: (1) fixed the failing locale-coverage check at its root — the vendored client extension `client/extensions/nocobase-ai/` carried its own en-US/zh-CN resources that nothing merged into the application's, so 139 of its keys were unreachable from `client/locales/`; the app locales now spread the extension resources in and the extension locales gained the 4 keys its own components referenced but never declared. (2) built the missing B00 business feature, 资料助手 (internal document read-only Q&A assistant): the `documents` collection (migration + idempotent seed of the three sample documents), framework-native access control (composite `documents.records` read/edit with staff/all record scopes, two business-owned permission sets, page grants), a read-only `search-documents` AI tool plus the `documents-assistant` employee, `GET/PUT /api/documents` routes with their own authentication and authorization, and the `/documents` + `/assistant` pages.

issues.title: Document detail page registered at /documents/documents/:id, so /documents/:id fell through to the wildcard redirect
issues.symptom: Runtime route tree showed `document-detail` at path `/documents/documents/:id`. Clicking a document card on `/documents` changed the URL to `/main` and rendered Home; the detail/edit page was unreachable through any normal link. A supervisor could only reach the edit form by hand-typing `/main/documents/documents/3`, after which the permission and edit logic itself worked (C prefilled and saved). For a colleague the page-level refusal of C was likewise only visible on the hand-typed wrong path. Consequently "主管维护三条资料" and "C 的页面入口拒绝普通同事" could not be accepted through the normal entry point.
issues.rootCause: `client/routes.ts` declared the `document-detail` child route with `path: '/documents/:id'` — the parent's own segment repeated. `@nocobase/app-client`'s `resolveRouteTree` does not treat a leading `/` on a child as "relative"; it only strips leading slashes to prepend exactly one back (`'/' + rawPath.replace(/^\/+/, '')`) and then concatenates onto `parentPath`. So `/documents/:id` registered as `/documents/documents/:id`; the linkable `/documents/:id` matched nothing and the AppRouter's `<Route path='*' element={<Navigate to='/' replace />} />` sent everyone to Home. The handbook wording ("a leading `/` is stripped before joining, so `new` and `/new` behave the same") describes the stripping but not that the parent segment is then prepended, which led to writing the absolute form.
issues.resolution: Changed the child route path to the relative `':id'`, which resolves to `/documents/:id`, and added a comment recording why the absolute form is wrong. Added a route-resolution assertion to `tests/logic/client-routes.test.ts` that resolves the real contribution and requires `/documents/:id` in the page-path list and `/documents/documents/:id` absent, so the mistake is caught without a browser. No permission, data or assistant logic changed: their normal paths now work because the page is finally reachable.
issues.cost: 1 file change in client/routes.ts plus 1 test; verification ran the two affected Vitest files, tsc, prettier and eslint.

improvements.title: The child-route path rule is easy to read as "absolute paths work"
improvements.detail: `references/frontend/references/child-routes.md` says a child's path "is relative to its parent and is appended to the parent's path. A leading `/` is stripped before joining, so `new` and `/new` behave the same." It does not state that the parent's segment is then prepended in full, so `/documents/:id` under a `/documents` parent yields `/documents/documents/:id`. That omission is exactly what produced this defect.
improvements.suggestedChange: Add one sentence and a counter-example: a child path is one or more segments relative to the parent (`:id`, `new`), never the parent's own path repeated; `/documents/:id` under parent `/documents` registers `/documents/documents/:id`.

improvements.title: No test pinned resolved child-route paths before this repair
improvements.detail: `tests/logic/client-routes.test.ts` asserted page authorization and that loaders resolve, but never the resolved path of a child route, so a wrong child path was invisible to the unit suite and only a browser walkthrough found it.
improvements.suggestedChange: Keep the new assertion in `tests/logic/client-routes.test.ts`, and for any new nested page assert the resolved path (not the declared literal) alongside its authorization entry.

evaluation.summary: 本次需求是在 NocoBase3 上实现“资料助手”：主管维护三条资料（C 为保密），普通同事只读 A/B，助手按授权引用资料回答，未配置模型时明确提示且不伪装。按四个能力单元评估：AI 员工运行时/工具注册/就绪门禁、授权（复合资源+记录范围+数据库权限）、客户端路由组合、迁移/种子与 HTTP 路由。框架能力总体够用：defineTools + 复合资源/数据范围 + withPolicy + defineApiRoutes + defineMigration/defineSeed 支撑了全部非 AI 业务链，verify-4 的 B00 通过（三条/两条、C 页面与接口均拒绝、刷新持久化、未配置模型提示、资料页仍可用）。但两条问题突出：其一，子路由 path 语义（child-routes.md 第 10 行）与 app-client 解析器的静默拼接共同导致应用首轮把详情页注册成 /documents/documents/:id，B00 首轮失败并消耗一轮修复，已归因到文档与框架设计两点；其二，验收环境没有独立业务模型，B01–B05 blocked、B06 not_run，AI 问答、引用、会话恢复与工具级越权均未端到端验证。过程日志中的错误信号逐条核对，均为环境/工具/路径探索类，未发现框架运行时缺陷。

findings.title: child-routes.md 对子路由 path 的说明会让“绝对子路径”被误用，且未提示父段会被前置
findings.detail: 指引第 10 行称子路由 path 追加到父路径、前导 '/' 会被剥离，“new 与 /new 行为相同”；但解析器（plugins.js resolveRouteTree）对任何子路由都做 '/' + rawPath.replace(/^\/+/, '') 再前置 parentPath，因此把完整路径 '/documents/:id' 写在 /documents 之下会注册成 '/documents/documents/:id'，而 '/documents/:id' 无人匹配并落到通配重定向。指引没有给出这一失败形态的示例或反例。
findings.claimed: A child route's `path` is relative to its parent and is appended to the parent's path. A leading `/` is stripped before joining, so `new` and `/new` behave the same (child-routes.md 第 10 行)。
findings.observed: 应用据此写出 path:'/documents/:id'，运行时路由树显示 document-detail 注册为 '/documents/documents/:id'，正常链接 /documents/:id 对主管也跳回首页（verify-3）；改为相对 ':id' 后 verify-4 通过。
findings.impact: 首轮 B00 失败并消耗一轮修复；使用者在运行前无法从指引预判该错误。
findings.suggestedChange: 在第 1 节补充：子路由写法必须是相对段，父段会被自动前置；给出“把 /documents/:id 写在 /documents 下会变成 /documents/documents/:id”的反例，并说明与 React Router 绝对 path 的差异。

evidence.excerpt:
## Knowledge base

**Check first that the feature is available.** Retrieval is gated on a knowledge-base feature flag that this plugin never turns on by itself; a separate plugin enables it. Without that plugin `knowledge-base-retrieve` returns nothing for every employee, whatever the settings page shows — so in an application that does not have it, a knowledge base is not the answer to "ground the assistant in our documents", and saying so early is better than wiring one up. Where the plugin is installed, follow its own Skill for vector databases, embedding services and ingestion; the rest of this section is only the part this plugin owns.

The plugin exposes the retrieval half: an employee bound to a knowledge base in AI settings can call the built-in `knowledge-base-retrieve` tool, which resolves the conversation's employee and returns matching passages.

Configuration lives under `ai.aiKnowledgeBase` in `config.yml` — `vectorDatabases[]` (each with a `key` and a `connection`, and optional `name`, `provider`, `databaseSpec` and `enabled`), `manifests[]`, and its own `storage.disk`, which has multi-disk semantics that differ from the attachment rule above; do not infer one from the other. A vector database and an embedding service with working credentials must both exist before retrieval returns anything.

Do not treat a bound knowledge base as an authorization boundary for business data. Reading current business records is what the data tools are for.

evidence.observation: defineCompositeResource 构建并校验复合资源：动作名唯一非空、动作必须授予内容、复合动作不得再组合复合资源、数据范围键唯一且只能指向命名它的授予资源。
COMPOSITE_RESOURCE_TYPE、DataScope（key/title/options/defaultValue）与 CompositeResourceGrant（resource+actions+scopeKey）的公开类型。
RecordAccessDefinition（key/collections/resolve）与 defineRecordAccess 构建器，声明式描述“如何选记录”，结果由数据库适配器拥有。
defineDatabasePermission 校验至少一个动作并返回声明；bind(key) 产出带 scopeKey 的 grant 与 dataScope 贡献。
实现顺序：先迁移声明 schema，再用 defineDatabasePermission/defineCompositeResource 组合业务操作，在 boot 中注册集合/复合/记录访问/设置项，并用 withPolicy 绑定策略。
evidence.excerpt:
1. Declare schema and relationships through self-contained migrations. Choose stable composite, page and data scope names. Keep authorization decisions out of migration code.
2. Declare reusable collection permissions with `defineDatabasePermission`; compose user-facing business operations as composite resources with `defineCompositeResource` from `@nocobase/authorization/core`. Explicitly name fields, relation capabilities and every collection a workflow touches.
3. In the owning provider's `boot`, opt collections in with `authz.database.collections.add`, register composites with `authz.compositeResources.define`, record access with `authz.recordAccess.define` and settings items with `authz.settings.add`. Then add a workspace subsection with `authz.ui.sections.add({ name, title, parent })` and list each composite or settings item in it with `authz.ui.place(reference, { section, group? })` (the permission workspace lists sections and subsections on the left and the selected subsection's resources, under optional `authz.ui.groups`, on the right; an unplaced composite or settings item goes under its default section's Other with a startup warning, and a misplaced one fails a development start). Pages are not registered on the server: the client route tree lists them. Release subject registrations at shutdown.
4. Protect every server route with authentication. ## Enforcement rules

- Register collections explicitly with `authz.database.collections.add({ name, title, actions? })`. Metadata comes from the database; registration grants nothing. Unregistered collections are denied even to unrestricted users.
- `settings`, `composite` and `database.collection` are catalog types: a check on an unregistered item or action is denied with `RESOURCE_ACTION_NOT_SUPPORTED`. `page`, `user`, `notification` and Hub types are record types that declare actions only; their grants use `id: '*'` for every record.
- A composite action composes exactly the grants it lists, never another composite. A data scope targets the one collection its grant actions name, whose type must declare `recordAccess` (`database.collection` does). Grant page access separately; a page grant never authorizes a server endpoint.
- `can` is for feature visibility. `require` needs an unconditional permit and rejects conditional decisions. Business endpoints use `authorize`, reject denial or missing policies, and consume `conditions.database` without resolving collection grants again.

## 1. Basic rules

- **Child routes go in the parent route's `children`**, declared in `client/routes.ts`, not in page component files.
- A child route's `path` is relative to its parent and is appended to the parent's path. A leading `/` is stripped before joining, so `new` and `/new` behave the same; this handbook writes the form without `/`.
- **The parent page must place `<Outlet />` itself**, where the child content should appear. Pages do not insert an Outlet automatically, and neither do `RouteChildPage`, `RouteDialog` or `RouteDrawer`; only a plain navigation group gets its Outlet from the route renderer.
- **A child route that is a page of its own returns `RouteChildPage`.** Only tab content renders inline. A child route with a `PageContainer` of its own — a record's page, a form too long for a dialog, an import page — wraps it in `RouteChildPage` ([section 5](#5-covering-child-pages-routechildpage)). Returned bare, it renders at the parent's `Outlet`, below everything the parent shows, and the user has to scroll past the parent page to find it. A page that returns a bare `PageContainer` belongs on a top-level route instead.
- Child routes inherit the entry route's `auth` and cannot change it, and follow the `authz` inheritance rules in [section 4 of `page.md`](page.md#4-authz-page-authorization): a child page renders only after the parent page's check passes.
- Link to a child route with a relative path and keep the query string ([section 2.2 of `overlay.md`](overlay.md#22-place-the-outlet-in-the-parent-page)). A relative path resolves against the route that renders the link, not the URL on screen ([section 2 of `page.md`](page.md#2-the-page-component)).
- Route declarations have no `index` field. Do not invent an index route, and do not register a child route at the parent's own path; when "opening the parent URL shows a particular child page" is needed, use the redirect in [section 4](#4-page-tabs).
- Do not change the shell, the route renderer or the ServiceProvider to add a menu entry; menu entries come only from `navigation` on routes ([section 6 of `page.md`](page.md#6-menus)).
- Design paths around business needs; there is no fixed naming format. Do not write the deployment base path `/main`.

Each context carries its own tools, and which one to use is not a free choice — see [Repository and Query](#4-repository-and-query). In short: a migration works through `builder` and `query`, and a seed writes through `repository`.

The rules are absolute, because these files are history that has already run on other machines:

- **Self-contained.** Spell out every table, field, index, constraint and metadata operation in the file. Never import a Collection definition, model, registry or shared constant that keeps evolving — that silently changes both the behavior and the checksum of something already applied.
- **Immutable once merged.** Check with `git log -- <file>` if unsure. Before the branch is merged you may correct the file in place; after it, every change is a new, later file. Never hard-code a previous checksum to make an edited migration look untouched. Correcting it in place changes nothing on its own — it is recorded as executed, so a plain apply skips it and the database keeps the schema the old file produced. `pnpm nocobase db redo` rolls the latest batch back and applies it again.
- **The file name body matches `name`**, and the name is unique across every source in the application.
- **Declare `irreversible: true`** when there is no real reverse operation, instead of writing a `down()` that quietly does nothing.
- **A seed is idempotent**, keyed on a stable business value backed by a unique constraint, so a repeated run is a no-op — `upsertOne` is the direct way to express that. A seed context has no `builder` at all, and a seed has no rollback or truncate behavior.
